input.strategy_title: Graduate Llama Stack to General Availability
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Llama Stack shipped as Tech Preview and adoption is strong, but enterprise
customers will not build production GenAI applications on a TP component.
Graduating to GA requires API stability commitments, a production support
posture, and closing the quality gaps that TP status currently excuses. The
full inventory of those gaps is not yet known — TP feedback is scattered across
support tickets, and no systematic GA-readiness assessment has been done.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current TP quality and GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), producing the definitive GA scope. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Published API surface carries a stability guarantee: versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases. |
| HLR-3 | P0 | Production support posture is in place: documented SLO targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix. |
| HLR-4 | P1 | Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions. |
| HLR-5 | P1 | The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate). |
| HLR-6 | P2 | Documentation is uplifted to GA standards, including migration notes from TP. |

## Affected Components

- Llama Stack
- TrustyAI
- Dashboard

## Out of Scope

- New Llama Stack feature development beyond GA-bar quality work
- Deprecating alternative GenAI serving paths

## Open Questions

1. The GA scope itself depends on HLR-1's assessment — until it lands, the
   size of the stability and hardening work is an estimate.

# GA-Readiness Assessment: Llama Stack TP-to-GA Gap Inventory and Definitive GA Scope

## Description

Resolves the strategy's gating unknown: Llama Stack shipped as Tech Preview
with strong adoption, but no systematic GA-readiness assessment has been done
and TP feedback is scattered across support tickets. This investigation
inventories the gaps between current TP quality and the GA bar — across API
stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, and error handling — and produces the
definitive GA scope against which all Llama Stack hardening work for the
graduation is planned.

## Scope

- Consolidate TP feedback from support tickets and other feedback channels into a single inventory
- Assess the current published API surface against the GA bar (versioning state, deprecation surface, breaking changes since the last two TP releases)
- Assess upgrade paths, including from the last two TP releases
- Assess scale limits and error-handling quality against production expectations
- Produce the definitive GA scope: an enumerated, severity-ranked gap list with a disposition per gap (fix-for-GA, accept, defer) and the hardening work required to close the fix-for-GA items

## Acceptance Criteria

- A GA-readiness report exists that enumerates gaps in each of the four dimensions (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), each with a severity and a disposition
- The gap inventory is grounded in consolidated TP support-ticket feedback and repository/API evidence, not anecdote
- The definitive GA scope is recorded and accepted by strategy stakeholders as the planning baseline for the graduation work
- Downstream hardening work (API stability guarantees, production support posture) can be scoped directly from the report without further discovery

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current TP quality and GA bar, producing the definitive GA scope

# Llama Stack API Stability Guarantees and Tested Upgrade Path

## Description

Delivers the published API surface stability guarantee required for GA: the
Llama Stack APIs carry versioning, a deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade
path from the last two TP releases. The epic's detailed scope is finalized
against the definitive GA scope produced by the GA-readiness assessment.

## Scope

- Version the published API surface (the OpenAI-compatible REST APIs and the LlamaStackDistribution CR) so GA consumers can pin against stable versions
- Define and publish a deprecation policy covering how breaking changes are announced and phased
- Implement and test upgrade paths from the last two TP releases
- Close the API-stability, upgrade-path, and error-handling gaps that the GA-readiness assessment dispositioned as fix-for-GA
- Add a rollback/compatibility safeguard for API changes where the strategy replaces TP-era behavior

## Acceptance Criteria

- The published API surface is versioned and ships with a documented deprecation policy
- Upgrades from each of the last two TP releases are executed and verified as passing, with documented evidence
- API-stability, upgrade-path, and error-handling gaps marked fix-for-GA in the GA-readiness assessment are closed, or their residual risk is explicitly accepted in the GA scope
- For every API change that replaces TP-era behavior, the rollback/compatibility safeguard is verified by an executed test showing the TP-era behavior is either preserved behind the documented compatibility mechanism or restorable via the tested rollback path, with the evidence recorded alongside that change's deprecation-policy entry
- No breaking change to the published surface ships outside the deprecation policy's process

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): Published API surface carries a stability guarantee — versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases

# Llama Stack Production Support Posture

## Description

Establishes the production support posture required for GA: documented SLO
targets, a backport policy, and a supported configuration matrix for Llama
Stack. The supported configuration matrix is finalized against the scale-limit
and error-handling findings of the GA-readiness assessment. These three
artifacts are the authoritative support-posture deliverables; the GA
documentation set integrates them as published rather than re-authoring them.

## Scope

- Define and publish the SLO targets as the authoritative support-posture artifact for production support of Llama Stack
- Define and publish the backport policy (which releases receive fixes, for how long) as the authoritative artifact
- Define and publish the supported configuration matrix — distributions, provider configurations, and scale limits supported at GA — as the authoritative artifact, incorporating the assessment's scale-limit and error-handling findings
- Align all three artifacts with the platform's standard GA support posture

## Acceptance Criteria

- SLO targets are documented and agreed with support and product stakeholders
- The backport policy is documented and published
- The supported configuration matrix is published and consistent with the scale-limit and error-handling findings of the GA-readiness assessment
- The three posture artifacts are complete for everything in the definitive GA scope

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P0): Production support posture in place — documented SLO targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix

# TrustyAI Guardrails as a Supported, Documented GA Integration

## Description

Promotes safety guardrails via TrustyAI from an experimental flag to a
supported, documented integration for GA distributions of Llama Stack. This is
GA-bar quality and support work on an existing integration, not new guardrails
feature development (which the strategy keeps out of scope).

## Scope

- Promote the TrustyAI guardrails integration from experimental-flag status to supported status for GA distributions of Llama Stack
- Harden the integration to GA-bar quality across the surfaces it touches (configuration, error handling, upgrade behavior)
- Author the TrustyAI guardrails integration documentation covering supported configuration, capabilities, and limitations — this epic owns that documentation as its deliverable; the GA documentation set uplifts and integrates it rather than re-authoring it
- Coordinate the integration surface across the TrustyAI operator and the Llama Stack distribution

## Acceptance Criteria

- The guardrails integration is available as a supported (non-experimental) integration in GA distributions of Llama Stack
- The integration is verified working on a supported GA configuration, including across an upgrade from the prior TP release
- Integration documentation is published covering configuration, capabilities, and limitations
- No remaining experimental-flag gating is required to enable the integration in a GA distribution

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P1): Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions

## Risks / Notes

- The work spans the TrustyAI operator and the Llama Stack distribution surface (owned by a different team); cross-team coordination is required. If substantial Llama Stack-distribution-side code work emerges, split it into a separate Llama Stack implementation epic blocked by this one.

# Dashboard Llama Stack Management Enabled by Default

## Description

Enables Llama Stack management in the Dashboard by default for entitled
clusters, removing the Tech Preview opt-in gate so entitled users get Llama
Stack management without action.

## Scope

- Change the Dashboard default so Llama Stack management is enabled on entitled clusters with no opt-in
- Remove the Tech Preview opt-in gate for entitled clusters
- Preserve a configuration-based rollback path: the Llama Stack Dashboard section remains disableable via the Dashboard's existing feature-flag mechanism
- Verify existing opt-in clusters continue to function after the default flip

## Acceptance Criteria

- On an entitled cluster with default configuration, Llama Stack management surfaces in the Dashboard with no opt-in action
- Clusters without entitlement do not surface Llama Stack management
- Disabling the Llama Stack Dashboard section via configuration is verified as a working rollback path
- Clusters that previously opted in continue to show Llama Stack management after the default change

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-5 (P1): The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate)

# Llama Stack GA Documentation Uplift and TP Migration Notes

## Description

Uplifts the Llama Stack documentation set to GA standards, including migration
notes from Tech Preview. Runs after all implementation work so the content
describes what was actually built and shipped for GA. Where deliverables are
owned elsewhere — the TrustyAI guardrails integration documentation authored by
the TrustyAI supported-integration work, and the support-posture artifacts (SLO
targets, backport policy, supported configuration matrix) published as
authoritative by the support-posture work — this epic integrates and uplifts
them into the GA documentation set rather than re-authoring them.

## Scope

Content outline:

- GA-standards uplift of the Llama Stack documentation set (accuracy, completeness, support statements)
- Migration notes from TP releases, covering the tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases
- Integration of the supported TrustyAI guardrails integration documentation into the GA documentation set: the TrustyAI supported-integration work authors the content (configuration, capabilities, limitations); this epic uplifts it to GA documentation standards, links it from the Llama Stack documentation, and strips any remaining experimental-flag framing
- Integration of the production support posture — SLO targets, backport policy, and the supported configuration matrix, published as the authoritative artifacts by the support-posture work — into the GA documentation set: surfaced, cross-linked, and presented consistently, not re-authored
- Updated guidance for default Dashboard enablement on entitled clusters, replacing TP opt-in instructions
- Removal or revision of TP-era caveats and experimental-flag instructions

## Acceptance Criteria

- The documentation set meets GA standards for accuracy and completeness
- Migration notes cover moving from TP releases (including the last two) to the GA release
- All content is technically reviewed against the implemented GA behavior by the owning engineers
- Each externally-owned deliverable — the TrustyAI guardrails integration documentation and the three support-posture artifacts (SLO targets, backport policy, supported configuration matrix) — appears in the GA documentation set exactly once, sourced from its owning deliverable with no duplicated or divergent re-authoring
- No TP-era experimental-flag or opt-in instructions remain in the GA documentation set

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-6 (P2): Documentation uplifted to GA standards, including migration notes from TP

strategy's single open question states that the GA scope itself depends on the
HLR-1 assessment — this makes the assessment a true gate for the hardening work.
